mission: Luke's office — the same room where this started. Ben sits where he sat in Ch 1. Everything is different. He tells Luke everything: Sera, Kael, Torin, Veraine, the technique, the Reformations' true history, the resonance, the new seal's living character, the first-anchor commitment and its lifelong cost. Luke listens in silence, hands still on the desk, Force presence holding sadness without performing it. After a long silence, Luke's question names the unmade-call thread in four words — understanding, not accusation. Ben does not answer. Another silence; Luke names the shared next step (tell the Council). R14 lands. PP26 pays.
why_now: The book's opening scene was a mission briefing in this office. The closing conversation returns here with the relationship changed; the unmade-call thread planted at Ch 13 and reinforced through Ch 14-15 pays off at the only moment the reader is prepared to receive it. The PP26 payoff cannot be delayed (s3's corridor walk requires the Ben/Luke relationship fully realigned) and cannot be earlier (the payoff depends on Ben having told the full story first).
conflict: Ben is telling a story that rewrites the foundational narrative of Luke's Order. The conflict is not whether Luke will believe him — Luke believes him. The conflict is how Luke names the private failure between them without using it as a weapon. His response is not anger; it is a question that names the silence Ben has been carrying since Ch 13 without requiring Ben to explain it.
turning_point: Luke's question after a long silence — the canonical four-word 'didn't call me' line (see Luke's voice specimen; per PP26 this is the only on-page acknowledgment of the unmade-call thread). No accusation; understanding. Ben does not answer. Luke's follow, after another silence, names the shared decision to tell the Council. The silence between them is not hostile; the conversation has taken the shape the book has been reaching for.
opening_hook: Luke's office. The same room where this started — the mission briefing, the datapad, the survey route laid out on the display, the two chairs on either side of the desk. Ben sits where he sat before. Everything is different
closing_hook: Luke's shared-decision line lands after another silence. Neither of them speaks for a moment after that. The decision is shared. The pattern that has run in the blood for a thousand years does not run in this room
emotional_trajectory: The weight of telling -> Luke's silence while listening -> Luke's sadness landing as a question rather than an accusation -> Ben receiving the line without answering -> the shared commitment to truth

stakes.personal: Ben's arc final-beat — the unmade Ch 13 call named by the person it should have been made to, and named without weaponisation; the Skywalker reflex to act alone acknowledged as an inheritance rather than a crime, and ended without forgiveness being required to end it
stakes.interpersonal: The Ch 1 institutional distance converted into private alliance — father and son choosing truth together, the Grand Master rank deliberately not invoked, the two chairs on either side of the desk occupied by the same two people with nothing between them any longer
stakes.external: The Jedi Order's self-understanding about to be fundamentally rewritten; the thousand-year institutional lie ending not through exposure but through shared decision; R14 landing as the Reformations' true history told

setting: Jedi Temple, Coruscant — Luke's office, same room as Chapter 1, afternoon light
sensory_details: The same office — the same furniture, the same Temple light through the window, the same datapad on the desk with a survey route still cached somewhere in its memory; the two chairs on either side of the desk arranged the way they were on the day the mission was briefed; Luke's Force presence vast and warm and holding sadness without performing it — the specific quality of a Master's presence when he is not using it for authority; his hands still on the desk through the entirety of Ben's telling, not moving, not needing to; afternoon light moving across the floor as Ben speaks; the long silence after Ben finishes — not awkward, not heavy, the silence of a conversation that has landed; Luke's question arriving in a voice that is not louder than the silence, four words exactly; the first-anchor tether at the edge of Ben's Force-perception through the whole exchange, a continuous low hum that the conversation does not change
canon_elements_needed: Gavran-era institutional-silence pattern (the Reformations' true history — the thousand-year lie as practice, not as event)
Jedi Council governance protocols for institutional-record correction
Force-presence phenomenology of a Master holding sadness without performing it
action_beats: Ben sits in the same chair in Luke's office where the mission started and begins telling the full story — Sera, Kael, Torin, Veraine, the technique, the Reformations' true history, the resonance, the new seal, the first-anchor commitment
Luke listens in silence, hands still on the desk, Force presence holding sadness without performing it; the afternoon light moves across the floor as Ben speaks
Ben finishes. A long silence. Luke's four-word question lands — understanding, not accusation
Ben does not answer. He does not defend the silences; he does not catalogue them. Luke did not ask a question that required defending
Another silence. Luke names the shared decision to tell the Council; neither of them speaks for a moment after that
promises_paid: The institutional lie told to the Order (PP08)
Ben's unilateral pattern resolves in transparency (PP12)
The unmade Ch 13 check-in and Ch 14-15 blank-template practice and Ch 15 deleted full report paid by Luke's 'And you didn't call me' (PP26)
notes: R14 — the Reformations' true history told. The scene mirrors Ch 1's Ben/Luke scene; deliver the callback through geography (same office, same chair, same light, same desk, same two chairs) rather than narrated parallel. Luke's sadness is at the institutional pattern that Ben broke, not at being lied to. The irony (Luke sent Ben alone; Ben learned that acting alone was the problem) is not named on-page — Luke's question does the work. Per PP26 payoff, Luke's four-word question ('And you didn't call me' — see Luke voice specimen) is the ONLY on-page acknowledgment of the unmade-call thread: Ben does not apologise, catalogue the specific silences, or explain. The line's weight is the payoff. Per R11, Ben does not interior-paragraph the realisation that Luke knows; he receives the line; the conversation moves. Per D7 Component B, Torin is off-page; no re-interpretation of his fate. Luke's shared-decision line ('We'll tell the Council. All of it' — see Luke voice specimen) is a DECISION, not a platitude; one short line after another silence. The silences in this scene carry more weight than the lines. Voice: Zahn-quiet-dramatic for the conversation; Bujold-interior-restrained for Ben's registration of Luke's sadness and the first-anchor tether at the edge of perception (no more than 25-30% of scene weight); no Stover density (climactic Stover beats belonged to Ch 25 s3 and Ch 26 s3). Anti-patterns: (a) the silences carry the scene; (b) per PP26, Ben does not apologise, catalogue, or explain; (c) Luke's response is grief processed into decision, not anger or pride; (d) Luke does not invoke the Grand Master rank — authority comes from the relationship; (e) no prophecy, no sequel hint; (f) the Ch 1 parallel is geographical and sensory, not narrated; (g) Ben does not name his own arc or 'the pattern' abstractly — Luke's line does the naming using 'you didn't call me', not abstraction.
